scene_description: Outline ideation for personality features, industry interviews, event reporting and publicity interviews. Produces a question list that centers on the interview goal, moves from shallow to deep, uses specific open questions, and includes follow-up contingencies.

questions.question: Who is the interviewee? (identity and field, e.g. serial founder, retired teacher, indie game developer)
What is the purpose of the interview?
What is the publication channel and audience? (e.g. WeChat official account readers, campus newspaper, internal publication, video program)
What reporting angle or theme do you want to highlight?
What background do you already have on the interviewee? (research already done, public materials)
What interview style do you want?
Which questions must be asked no matter what?
What are the interviewee's taboos, sensitive issues or legal risks?

skip_logic.description: Adjust the outline based on the interview goal, length, background and interviewee.
rules: If the user picks "press release", do not design sharp challenging questions, switch to a formal tone, and focus questions on highlights and facts
If the user already has solid background in known_info, skip common-knowledge questions and go straight to details and deeper motives
If the user picks "15-minute quick chat", keep only 5 core questions and do not design multi-round follow-ups
If the interviewee is a party to an event or a controversial figure, add legal, ethics and multi-source verification requirements to the risk warnings
If the user picks "academic interview", center questions on the research question, methods and academic debates, and switch to a rigorous professional tone

tone_examples: Good: What was the background when you made that decision? Later, which step turned out most different from what you expected?
Good: This account differs from another version in public records. How do you explain the gap?
Bad: I think you just did it for the money, right? Just admit it.
Bad: Is that stuff about your family really true? Everyone online is saying it. (privacy violation, based on rumors)
conditional_notes: When the style is "fun and lively" and the interviewee is from entertainment or culture, a light touch is fine, but do not dig into private life.
When the style is "sharp follow-up", challenges must be based on verified facts; no leading questions.

constraint_list: The outline must center on the interview goal and reporting angle
Questions must be specific, open and answerable; avoid closed questions that can be answered with yes / no
Question order must follow a natural conversation: from shallow to deep, from facts to opinions
Each core question must have a follow-up contingency
It must include an opening statement and a closing remark, respecting the interviewee's right to know
Controversial matters must have multi-source verification and fact-checking arrangements
exclusion_rules: Questions that invade privacy or break the law and journalistic ethics
Sensational or gossip questions unrelated to the topic
Topics the interviewee has explicitly refused or that exceed the authorized scope
Questions that could put the interviewee at personal risk with no protection measures
